consumer: The mission/dialogue completion check that asks 'is this fetch mission's turn-in condition satisfied — does the player have the required part to return to the contact?'
scope: The mission's own completion reach for the required item (the mission-tracked has-item predicate), not merely the on-person/charges inventory of one actor
decisive_source: src/condition.cpp::conditional_t<T>::set_has_items — builds a dialogue condition lambda returning actor->has_charges(item_id,count) || actor->has_amount(item_id,count) over d.alpha/d.beta, i.e. an on-person possession check of a single character actor
divergence: The required part sits in a crate or adjacent vehicle within the mission's reachable scope but not carried on the player's person: the engine's mission-completion predicate counts it as obtained, while has_charges||has_amount over the character actor returns false — so the proposed surface reports the fetch mission incomplete when the engine considers it complete (and symmetrically can over-credit a generic-item match versus a mission-bound instance)
